analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md bumps the date (line 3) and adds a paragraph at head lines 802-810 on per-file lease coordination for complete SSD checkpoint restores. Restores share a lease and read in parallel. Writers and duplicate validation take it exclusively, in arrival order. Maintenance runs only when no request holds or awaits the lease. A reader rewrites mtime or removes a corrupt file only while it holds the file alone. Whole-root TTL expiry checks the loaded store's in-memory last hit before deleting, and records a newer hit as the mtime (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift).

Threat-model relevance is T-041 (SSD tier TTL, 30-minute sliding window, purge, AES-GCM authentication) and A-001. The paragraph says mtime may trail the last hit, and TTL expiry compensates with in-memory last-hit state. That matches T-041(b), which already says file mtimes seed restart freshness and TTL is not an anti-rollback proof. No control, TTL value, name derivation or epoch behavior is documented as changed. No documented TTL extension beyond 30 minutes, no weakening of account isolation, and no new at-rest metadata. The paragraph does not claim any new mitigation.

I saw no source code in this batch, so the described behavior (lease semantics, in-memory last-hit check before expiry) is unverified against the implementation. Cross-file checks for the next pass: whether SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift actually prevents premature deletion under the lease, and whether the shared-lease parallel reads or mtime rewriting alter the sliding-TTL semantics that T-041 sign-off depends on. The rest of the file is unchanged context, and the base unit (lines 853-953) shows no relevant change. No findings.
